newsitem.title: INDIA: World Bank chief starts India tour in Bombay slums.
newsitem.headline: World Bank chief starts India tour in Bombay slums.

text.p: World Bank president James Wolfensohn started a weeklong tour of India in Bombay on Sunday by visiting one of Asia's worst slums to see how the bank's money was being used to improve living standards.
India, with around $15 billion a year in World Bank loans, and is the largest recipient of the bank's money.
Finance Minister P.Chidambaram met Wolfensohn in Washington earlier this month and called for the bank to double its lending to India to help the country overcome chronic infrastructure problems.

Wolfensohn will discuss capital market developments and infrastructure financing with industry leaders, and meet central bank governor Chakravarty Rangarajan and Maharashtra state chief minister Manohar Joshi on Monday.

On Sunday he went to housing and sanitation projects run by non-government in the slum area of Dharavi and on Monday plans to see for himself the the bedlam of Bombay's main Churchgate railway station at rush hour.

He plans to visit the city's infamous red light district to see what measures are being taken to counter the spread of AIDS, and other health and population control programmes are also on his agenda on Monday.

Wolfensohn will leave for the southern city of Bangalore on Monday evening to participate in a business roundtable organised by the International Finance Corporation. On Wednesday he goes to Bhubaneshwar in the eastern state of Orissa, where World bank funds have been used to restructure its power sector.

Wolfensohn will spend the final three days of his tour, October 17-19, in New Delhi, where he will meet Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, finance minister Chidambaram, and President Shanker Dayal Sharma.
